title: Why You Need A Good Relationship With Difficult Students cult-students/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin contends that merely refraining from hurtful methods with difficult students isn't enough—teachers must actively cultivate a relationship these students come to appreciate. He explains that a good relationship supplies the leverage that makes consequences meaningful, since accountability means nothing to a student who resents the teacher. He also argues that warmth and consistency soften a difficult student's guard and strip away damaging labels like 'troublemaker' that these students otherwise internalize and fulfill. The piece insists this effort must come from the teacher first, without expectation of an immediate return, even while enduring initial pushback or disrespect.
points: Time-out and other consequences carry no weight with a student who dislikes or resents the teacher; likability creates the leverage that makes accountability work.
A trusted relationship 'softens the heart,' opening students to feedback and humor they would otherwise reject.
Unconditional friendliness helps strip away self-fulfilling labels like 'behavior problem' or 'troublemaker.'
Building the relationship is entirely the teacher's responsibility and must be offered first, often while enduring disrespect in return.
Once difficult students begin to feel like regular members of the class, they begin behaving like regular members of the class.
quotes: Most teachers have a less-than positive relationship with difficult students—although it isn’t always evident to those around them.
The leverage you need to compel them to behave comes from your likability and general pleasantness. When they like you and trust you, they’ll want to please you.
Difficult students expect you to glare at them. They expect sarcasm. They expect you to be like all the rest.
They have an irresistible inclination to fulfill those labels, to become what is reinforced day after day.
Having a good relationship with difficult students is a choice you make that is 100% in your power to control. But it must come from you first.
You’ll have an opportunity to climb through the rubble, walk unchallenged past their defenses, and speak in both word and example directly into their heart.
